# Company 089 — Automated Support-QA Platform

**Company ID:** `company:future:089`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:089`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-089-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no employee discipline, customer contact or production support action.

## Business identity
Purpose: evaluate human and AI customer-support interactions for correctness, policy, security, privacy, tone, resolution quality and operational outcomes at near-complete coverage.

## Product tree
Conversation Ingest; Rubric/Policy Builder; Correctness Evaluator; Policy/Compliance QA; Security/Privacy QA; Tone/Empathy QA; Resolution/First-Contact QA; Escalation QA; Hallucination/Promise Detection; Sentiment/Customer Effort; Handle-Time/Repeat-Contact Analytics; AI-vs-Human Comparison; Scorecards; Coaching Recommendations; Calibration Workspace; Dispute/Appeal; Workforce Analytics; QA Sampling/Full-Coverage; API/SDK; Enterprise/Private Deployment; Vertical Support Packs.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree
Features: channel, agent/human/model identity, queue/product, customer issue, policies/knowledge versions, actions/promises, citations, escalation, resolution outcome, sentiment, handling time, repeat contact, QA dimensions, confidence, evidence spans, reviewer calibration and appeal.
Customers: support organizations, SaaS, ecommerce, marketplaces, contact centers, BPOs, AI support vendors, enterprises and regulated service providers.
Verticals: software support, ecommerce, telecom-like service, financial/health administrative support, travel/hospitality, marketplaces and technical support.

## Brain capability / architecture
Evaluation may require LLM/judge models but must be grounded in exact knowledge/policy versions, calibrated against human review and separated from employment decisions. Deterministic checks should cover prohibited promises, missing disclosures, authentication steps and measurable metrics. Architecture: interaction store/ref, policy/KB snapshot, rubric registry, evaluator ensemble, deterministic rule checks, calibration set, appeals/review, analytics and provenance.

## Agent tree
Ingest Agent; Policy QA Agent; Correctness Agent; Security/Privacy Agent; Tone Agent; Resolution Agent; Escalation Agent; Hallucination Agent; Calibration Agent; Coaching Agent; Trend Analyst; QA Governance Agent.

## Deterministic services
PII redaction; channel normalization; policy/version binding; keyword/action rules; metric calculation; sampling; confidence thresholds; reviewer assignment; score versioning; appeal/recalculation; access control.

## Workflow
Interaction closes → redact/classify → bind exact policy/KB/rubric version → deterministic checks → model-based evaluated dimensions → confidence/calibration → score/evidence → route uncertain/high-impact cases to human reviewer → publish QA result/coaching → appeal/review if needed → aggregate trends without silently disciplining workers.

## Integrations / API / data
Helpdesk/contact-center systems, chat/email/voice transcripts, CRM, knowledge bases, policy stores, AI support platforms, workforce systems and analytics. Data: interactions, policy snapshots, evaluations, evidence spans, calibrations, appeals and trends.

## Monetization / distribution
Interactions/minutes, agents, channels, seats, enterprise/private, compliance packs, API and managed QA. Distribution via support/contact-center/BPO/AI-support ecosystems.

## Security/privacy/compliance
Support conversations contain sensitive customer data. Redaction, role-based access, retention, human review for employment/high-impact decisions, bias calibration and no secret customer data in model training without consent.

## Failure / edge cases
Wrong policy version, sarcastic language, ambiguous resolution, customer misinformation, multiple agents, transferred ticket, missing transcript segment, voice transcription error, regional policy variation, justified policy exception, customer sentiment not caused by agent, AI judge drift.

## Scale / overlap
Team QA → enterprise full-coverage QA → support-quality infrastructure. Overlap #45 autonomous support and #3 AI QC. #089 owns support-interaction quality.

## Classification
**DESIGN NOW:** evaluator versioning, policy/knowledge snapshot provenance, human calibration, confidence/evidence spans and high-impact decision separation.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center Evaluation Factory should already support judge/evaluator calibration and versioned reference truth.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** customer transcript ingest, support rubrics and calibration infrastructure.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** support connectors/vertical packs/workforce UI.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** massive real-time multimodal support QA.

# Mandatory 24-part completion block
1. Product Tree: ingest/rubrics/correctness/policy/security/tone/resolution/escalation/hallucination/sentiment/analytics/comparison/scorecards/coaching/calibration/API.
2. Feature Tree: channel/agent/issue/policy-KB version/actions/promises/citations/escalation/outcome/sentiment/time/repeat/evidence/calibration.
3. Customer Tree: support/SaaS/ecommerce/marketplace/contact center/BPO/AI support/enterprise/regulated.
4. Vertical Tree: software/commerce/telecom-like/finance admin/health admin/travel/marketplace/technical support.
5. Brain Tree: grounded evaluation; high-impact employment decisions excluded.
6. Agent Tree: ingest/policy/correctness/security/tone/resolution/escalation/hallucination/calibration/coaching/trends/governance.
7. Service Tree: redaction/normalize/version binding/rules/metrics/sampling/thresholds/reviewer/score version/appeal.
8. Workflow Tree: close→redact→bind truth→checks/eval→calibrate→review→score/coaching→appeal/trends.
9. Integration Tree: helpdesk/contact center/chat/email/voice/CRM/KB/policy/AI support/workforce.
10. Data Tree: interactions/policy snapshots/evals/evidence/calibration/appeals/trends.
11. API Tree: interactions/evaluate/scores/evidence/calibration/trends.
12. Monetization Tree: interactions/minutes/agents/channels/seats/enterprise/API/managed.
13. Distribution Tree: support/contact-center/BPO/AI-support/OEM.
14. Automation Tree: QA/coaching/trends automatic; high-impact HR/customer actions separate.
15. Moat Tree: calibrated QA corpus, vertical rubrics, policy-version grounding, multimodal coverage.
16. Platform Tree: QA scorecard→full coverage support QA→customer-service quality infrastructure.
17. Risk Tree: judge bias/wrong policy/privacy/employment harm/false hallucination/transcript error.
18. Scale Tree: team→enterprise→real-time multimodal fleet.
19. Spinoff Tree: coaching/calibration modules; general AI QC and support execution remain separate.
20. Command Center Dependencies: evaluations, policy/KB snapshots, redaction, identity, analytics, provenance.
21. Design-Now Requirements: evaluator outputs must carry model/rubric/reference versions and confidence/evidence.
22. Build-Now Requirements: Evaluation Factory should support independent calibrated judges and appeal/review states.
23. Safe-to-Defer Requirements: customer support connectors/workforce dashboards/commercial rubrics.
24. Autonomous Mature State: every interaction is evaluated and trends/coaching generated; humans calibrate rubrics and adjudicate uncertain/high-impact findings.

## Saturation result
Further branches converge into AI QC, autonomous support and general analytics already represented.

# Company 090 — Content Moderation Infrastructure API

**Company ID:** `company:future:090`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:090`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-090-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no user-content enforcement, account sanction or live platform moderation.

## Business identity
Purpose: provide configurable real-time and batch content-policy classification, routing, human review and appeal infrastructure for platforms handling user-generated text, images, video and audio.

## Product tree
Text Moderation API; Image Moderation; Video Moderation; Audio/Voice Moderation; Live Stream Sampling; URL/Link Scanner; Profile/Username/Metadata Checks; Spam/Scam Detection; Harassment/Abuse; Sexual/Violence/Illegal-Content Taxonomies; Platform Custom Policy Builder; Age/Regional Policy Packs; Confidence/Threshold Engine; Human Review Queue; Appeal Workflow; Case Management; Audit/Transparency Reports; Batch Moderation; SDK/Edge Gateway; Enterprise/Private Deployment; Reviewer Tooling.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree
Features: content ID/version/source, creator/account ref, modality, language/region, policy taxonomy/version, label probabilities, severity, context, confidence, threshold, automated/human decision, reviewer, appeal, evidence, action recommendation and enforcement receipt reference.
Customers: marketplaces, communities, social platforms, games, creator platforms, messaging services, education/community tools and enterprise user-content products.
Verticals vary heavily by audience, age, jurisdiction and product policy. Policies must be platform-owned and versioned.

## Brain capability / architecture
Multimodal ML/LLM/classifiers may assist labeling; deterministic policy maps labels/confidence/context to review/action classes. High-impact/account sanctions need appeal/review controls. Architecture: ingestion, multimodal classifier router, policy taxonomy/version registry, context service, threshold engine, human-review queue, appeal/case ledger, evaluation/calibration and privacy controls.

## Agent tree
Content Classifier; Spam/Scam Agent; Harassment Agent; Safety Taxonomy Agent; Context Agent; Human Review Router; Appeal Agent; Policy QA Agent; Model Calibration Agent; Incident/Abuse Trend Agent; Transparency Reporting Agent.

## Deterministic services
Hash/dedup; media preprocessing; age/region/policy resolution; thresholds; rate limits; review assignment; decision versioning; action recommendation schema; appeal state; retention; audit and model/evaluator versioning.

## Workflow
Content event → validate/source bind → preprocess → run modality classifiers → apply exact platform policy/version + context → auto-allow/review/restrict recommendation according to threshold → human review for required classes → downstream platform enforcement separately authorized → user appeal if offered → re-review → feed calibrated evaluation and transparency metrics.

## Integrations / API / data
Platforms, storage/CDN, identity/account systems, human-review vendors, trust/safety case tools, law-enforcement/legal workflows only where lawfully authorized, analytics and SIEM. Data: content refs/hashes, labels, policies, decisions, reviews, appeals and metrics; minimize retention of harmful/private raw content.

## Monetization / distribution
Requests/items/minutes/GB, reviewer seats, policy packs, enterprise/private, API/SDK and managed moderation operations. Distribution via platform/dev/security ecosystems.

## Security/privacy/compliance
Avoid overcollection, child/minor privacy risks, reviewer exposure, classifier bias and unsupported legal claims. Strong access controls, reviewer safety, audit, regional policy, appeals, transparency and prohibition on abusive censorship tooling beyond customer/platform lawful policy.

## Failure / edge cases
Satire/quotation, reclaimed slurs, educational/news context, multilingual slang, coded language, image-text combinations, live latency, adversarial cropping, false positives, coordinated brigading, appeals, minors, local law conflicts, platform-specific allowed content, model drift.

## Scale / overlap
API → platform trust/safety stack → multimodal moderation infrastructure. Overlap #57 fraud, #67 injection firewall, #89 support QA. #090 owns user-content policy moderation.

## Classification
**DESIGN NOW:** policy/version, confidence/evidence, human review/appeal, model/evaluator version, tenant isolation and action-vs-classification separation.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center Evaluation/Policy engines can reuse generic classification→policy→review patterns but must not import customer content.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** multimodal classifiers, policy builder, review/appeal infrastructure.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** customer policy packs/reviewer operations/pricing.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** global low-latency multimodal moderation and reviewer networks.

7. Service Tree: hash/preprocess/policy resolution/threshold/rate/reviewer/decision/appeal/retention/audit/versioning.
8. Workflow Tree: ingest→classify→policy→auto/review recommendation→human where needed→enforcement ref→appeal→calibrate.
9. Integration Tree: platform/storage/identity/review vendors/case tools/analytics/SIEM.

13. Distribution Tree: platform/dev/security/OEM.
14. Automation Tree: classification/routing automatic; high-impact enforcement/review policy-controlled.
15. Moat Tree: calibrated multimodal models, policy tooling, appeal outcomes, language/context coverage.
16. Platform Tree: moderation API→trust/safety stack→content-governance infrastructure.
17. Risk Tree: bias/overmoderation/undermoderation/privacy/reviewer harm/legal mismatch/model drift.
18. Scale Tree: API→platform→global multimodal network.
19. Spinoff Tree: reviewer tooling/appeal service; injection/fraud/support QA stay separate.

# Company 091 — AI Agent Identity & Trust Authority

**Company ID:** `company:future:091`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:091`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-091-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no external identity issuance, credential provisioning, cross-company trust or machine authority grant.

## Business identity
Purpose: provide verifiable identity, credential, delegation, ownership and trust records for autonomous software agents and their runtime instances.

Problem: agentic systems need to answer who an agent is, who owns it, what exact version/runtime is acting, who delegated authority, what it may do, how long authority lasts and whether its trust has changed.

Value: machine-verifiable agent passports, scoped delegation, revocation, accountability and cross-system trust without treating a model name or API token as identity.

## Complete product tree
Agent Identity Registry; Organization/Owner Identity Binding; Agent/Brain/Model/Runtime/Version Identity; Instance/Session Identity; Task-Scoped Identity; Credential Issuance; Temporary/Scoped Credentials; Signed Assertions; Agent Certificates/Passports; Delegation Chain Engine; Authority Scope Registry; Spending/Tool/Data/Communication Limits; Expiry/Revocation; Reputation/Trust Score; Behavior/Incident History; Cross-Organization Trust Relationships; Authentication Gateway; Verification API; Developer SDK; Enterprise Private CA/Authority; Agent Marketplace Trust Profile; Lifecycle/Retirement; Federation/Interoperability.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree
Features: stable agent ID, owner/org, creator/build provenance, brain/model/version, runtime/environment, instance/session, parent/delegator, scope/resource/actions, budgets, time/region/task restrictions, credential refs, signatures, attestation, incidents, trust/reputation, revocation/suspension and lifecycle.
Customers: agent platforms, enterprises, AI SaaS, marketplaces, developer ecosystems, machine-to-machine platforms, security/IAM vendors and regulated organizations.
Verticals: software agents, financial-operation agents, browser agents, support agents, procurement agents, infrastructure agents and cross-company agent networks.

## Brain capability / architecture
Trust reasoning may analyze behavior/incident evidence, but identity/credential/delegation verification must be cryptographic/deterministic. Architecture: globally stable identifier scheme, ownership registry, certificate/assertion service, KMS/vault, delegation graph, policy/authority records, runtime attestation hooks, revocation service, trust/reputation event ledger and federation protocol.

## Agent tree
Identity Provisioning Agent; Ownership Verification Agent; Credential Lifecycle Agent; Delegation Auditor; Runtime Attestation Agent; Trust/Reputation Analyst; Incident/Revocation Agent; Federation Agent; Policy QA Agent; Developer Support Agent.

## Deterministic services
Identifier issuance; key/cert generation refs; signature verification; scope subset checks; delegation depth; expiry; nonce/replay prevention; credential rotation; revocation lists/status; chain validation; signed attestations; trust-event hashes.

## Workflow tree
Owner/org authorizes identity → create stable agent identity tied to build/brain/runtime metadata → issue scoped credential/attestation → parent delegates subset authority for exact task → verifier checks identity/chain/scope/expiry/revocation → agent acts only through downstream policy gate → outcomes/incidents append trust evidence → rotate/suspend/revoke/retire without rewriting history.

## Integrations / API / data
IAM/SSO, KMS/vault, agent frameworks, model gateways, runtime/security gateways, tool providers, marketplaces, billing/commerce gateways, audit/SIEM. Data: identity/delegation/certificate metadata, scopes, trust events and revocation; private keys remain protected outside normal app data.

## Monetization / distribution
Agent identities, verifications, credential operations, trust lookups, enterprise/private authority, federation, SDK/API and certification programs. Distribution through AI-agent/IAM/security/developer ecosystems.

## Security/privacy/compliance
Identity authority is critical root infrastructure. Strong key protection, owner verification, anti-impersonation, replay defense, revocation propagation, no trust score without explainable evidence, no uncontrolled cross-company correlation and strict separation between identity and permission decisions.

## Failure / edge cases
Cloned agent, compromised runtime, stolen credential, model upgraded without identity version change, owner org changes, delegation chain too deep, clock skew, offline verifier, key compromise, malicious reputation report, cross-company naming collision, retired agent resurrected, task credential reused.

## Scale / overlap
Single enterprise registry → federated agent identity → potential trust layer for agentic internet. Overlap #2 control center, #4 permissions, #66 security gateway, #73 credential rotation, #92 commerce. #091 owns agent identity/delegation/trust primitive.

## Classification
**DESIGN NOW:** stable agent/brain/model/runtime/instance IDs, owner/delegator provenance, subset-only scopes, expiry/revocation, credential refs and trust-event evidence.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center Agency already has logical Project Agent/worker identities; reverse-map says these need a unified machine-identity envelope now rather than later retrofit.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** external/federated agent credentials and portable verification.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** commercial authority/marketplace trust network.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** global federation/reputation network.

# Company 092 — Agentic Commerce Transaction Gateway

**Company ID:** `company:future:092`  
**Primary project:** `project:company:future:092`  
**Roadmap version:** `COMPANY-092-v1.0.0`  
**Truth state:** PLANNED  
**Authorization:** roadmap/architecture only; no purchase, card/payment issuance, merchant commitment, refund or financial transaction.

## Business identity
Purpose: allow autonomous agents to initiate commerce only inside explicit identity, delegation, budget, merchant, item, price, quantity, tax, fraud and approval constraints with receipts and reconciliation.

## Product tree
Agent Buyer Identity Adapter; Merchant Identity/Trust; Purchase Intent Schema; Budget/Spend Policy; Merchant/SKU Allow-Deny; Quote Comparison; Machine-Readable Offer/Cart; Approval Thresholds; Virtual/Scoped Payment Credential Adapter; Transaction Authorization Gateway; Receipt/Invoice Capture; Subscription/Renewal Controls; Refund/Return Workflow; Dispute Workflow; Tax/Shipping Handoff; Procurement Mode; Travel/Expense Mode; Digital/API Purchase Mode; Recurring Purchase Scheduler; Reconciliation; Audit/Provenance; API/SDK; Enterprise/Private Deployment; Merchant Agent Protocol.

## Feature/customer/vertical tree
Features: agent/owner/company identity, delegation chain, purchase purpose/task, merchant identity, product/SKU/service, quote/version, price/currency/tax/shipping, quantity, budget/cost center, allowed categories, recurring terms, approval threshold, payment credential ref, transaction ID, receipt, refund/dispute and evidence.
Customers: enterprises, agent platforms, procurement systems, travel/expense platforms, API/software buyers, marketplaces and machine-to-machine commerce providers.
Verticals: office/business supplies, SaaS/API purchasing, cloud/compute, travel booking, procurement, marketplace/digital goods and replenishment. High-risk/regulatory categories may be prohibited.

## Brain capability / architecture
Brain may search/compare offers and recommend purchases; deterministic policy must enforce budget, merchant/SKU/category, quantity, price ceiling and approval. Money movement is never inferred from conversational intent alone. Architecture: agent identity/delegation, merchant/product offer schema, budget ledger, purchase-intent record, policy/risk/fraud gate, approval broker, payment-provider abstraction, receipt/provenance ledger and reconciliation.

## Agent tree
Purchase Planner; Quote Comparison Agent; Merchant Trust Agent; Budget Agent; Procurement Agent; Subscription/Renewal Agent; Receipt Agent; Refund/Return Coordinator; Dispute Agent; Reconciliation Agent; Fraud/Security Agent; QA/Compliance Agent.

## Deterministic services
Budget arithmetic; cost-center limits; merchant/category/SKU rules; price/quantity ceilings; recurring commitment parser; one-time authorization; idempotent purchase intent/transaction; payment credential token refs; receipt matching; refund/chargeback state; audit.

## Workflow tree
Task needs purchase → create immutable purchase intent → verify agent identity/delegation → discover/compare eligible offers → freeze merchant/SKU/price/terms → policy/budget/fraud/tax/shipping checks → step-up approval if required → create scoped payment authorization → execute once through provider → capture receipt/order → verify fulfillment → reconcile ledger → handle return/refund/dispute under separate authority.

## Integrations / API / data
Agent identity, procurement catalogs, merchants/marketplaces, payment processors/virtual-card providers, billing/expense systems, tax/shipping, order/fulfillment, accounting and fraud services. Data: intents, offers, policies, budgets, approvals, transaction refs, receipts, fulfillment and reconciliation; raw payment secrets never stored in normal app state.

## Monetization / distribution
Transaction/gateway fees, agent/company subscriptions, purchase volume, enterprise/private, API/SDK, merchant integrations and compliance/security packs. Distribution through agent platforms, procurement/payment ecosystems and merchants.

## Security/privacy/compliance
Extremely high financial risk. Hard spend limits, merchant/category controls, no hidden subscriptions, explicit recurring terms, fraud checks, scoped credentials, separation of requester/approver where required, no purchase from untrusted content alone, full audit and emergency kill switch. Financial/licensing/regulatory obligations vary by role and jurisdiction.

## Failure / edge cases
Price changes after approval, partial fulfillment, duplicate transaction, merchant fraud, counterfeit item, tax/shipping changes, subscription auto-renew, unavailable SKU substitution, agent retries after timeout, refund to wrong instrument, card credential leak, cross-company purchase, ambiguous product, dynamic travel fares.

## Scale / overlap
Internal agent purchasing → enterprise agent commerce → potential agentic financial rails. Overlap #4 permissions, #66 security gateway, #69 billing, #91 identity/trust, #32 procurement. #092 owns autonomous transaction gateway.

## Classification
**DESIGN NOW:** immutable action/purchase intents, agent/delegation identity, budget/cost-center scopes, one-time authorization, receipts/reconciliation, merchant/resource identity, recurring-commitment class.  
**BUILD NOW:** Command Center Financial/Policy Governors and protected-action gate should support exact purchase intents and budgets even though spending remains unauthorized.  
**BUILD BEFORE FIRST COMPANY:** external merchant/payment adapters and customer procurement policies.  
**COMPANY-SPECIFIC LATER:** transaction product, merchant network and regulated payment rails.  
**SCALE-ONLY:** global agent-commerce protocol/network.

# Mandatory 24-part completion block
1. Product Tree: identity/merchant/intent/budget/SKU rules/quotes/offers/approval/payment/receipts/subscriptions/refunds/disputes/tax/procurement/travel/API.
2. Feature Tree: agent/delegation/purpose/merchant/SKU/offer/price/tax/quantity/budget/terms/approval/payment ref/receipt/evidence.
3. Customer Tree: enterprise/agent platform/procurement/travel/API buyers/marketplace/M2M.
4. Vertical Tree: supplies/SaaS-API/cloud/travel/procurement/digital/replenishment.
5. Brain Tree: search/compare/recommend; spending enforcement deterministic and approval-bound.
6. Agent Tree: planner/quotes/merchant trust/budget/procurement/subscription/receipt/refund/dispute/reconcile/security/QA.
7. Service Tree: budgets/rules/ceilings/terms/idempotency/one-time auth/payment refs/receipt match/refund state/audit.
8. Workflow Tree: need→intent→identity→offers→freeze→policy/budget→approve→execute once→receipt→fulfill/reconcile.
9. Integration Tree: identity/catalogs/merchants/payments/expense/tax/shipping/orders/accounting/fraud.
10. Data Tree: intents/offers/policies/budgets/approvals/transactions/receipts/fulfillment/reconciliation.
11. API Tree: intents/offers/authorize/execute status/receipts/refunds/reconcile.
12. Monetization Tree: transactions/volume/agents/companies/enterprise/API/merchant integrations.
13. Distribution Tree: agents/procurement/payments/merchants/OEM.
14. Automation Tree: comparison/policy/receipts automatic; money movement approval-bound.
15. Moat Tree: merchant/product schemas, risk controls, transaction outcome graph, agent interoperability.
16. Platform Tree: purchase gateway→agent commerce rails→machine commerce network.
17. Risk Tree: unauthorized spend/duplicate/subscription trap/fraud/wrong item/cross-company leak/regulatory exposure.
18. Scale Tree: company purchasing→enterprise→cross-merchant agentic network.
19. Spinoff Tree: purchase-intent standard/merchant trust/receipt reconciliation; identity and procurement remain separate.
20. Command Center Dependencies: machine identity, financial governor, protected actions, resource governor, secrets, reconciliation, incidents.
21. Design-Now Requirements: purchase/spend intents must be exact, immutable, scoped, budgeted and separately authorized.
22. Build-Now Requirements: add generic budget/cost-center/purchase-intent semantics to Command Center governance without enabling spend.
23. Safe-to-Defer Requirements: payment rails/merchant network/virtual cards/regulated operations.
24. Autonomous Mature State: agents source and prepare compliant purchases automatically; money executes only inside hard budgets/policies/approval classes and reconciles automatically.

## Saturation result
Further branches converge into procurement, identity/trust, runtime security, billing and payment reconciliation already represented.
